arxiv-1706-08152.title: An algorithm to find maximum area polygons circumscribed about a convex polygon
arxiv-1706-08152.creator: Markus Ausserhofer, Susanna Dann, Zsolt Lángi and Géza Tóth
arxiv-1706-08152.description: Abstract . A convex polygon Q Q is circumscribed about a convex polygon P P if every vertex of P P lies on at least one side of Q Q . We present an algorithm for finding a maximum area convex polygon circumscribed about any given convex n n -gon in O ⁡ ( n 3 ) O(n^{3}) time.

arxiv-2112-12335.title: Primordial black hole formation from massless scalar isocurvature
arxiv-2112-12335.creator: Chul-Moon Yoo, Tomohiro Harada, Shin’ichi Hirano, Hirotada Okawa, Misao Sasaki
arxiv-2112-12335.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chul-Moon Yoo, Tomohiro Harada, Shin’ichi Hirano, Hirotada Okawa, Misao Sasaki. We numerically study the primordial black hole (PBH) formation by an isocurvature perturbation of a massless scalar field on super Hubble scales in the radiation-dominated universe. As a first step we perform simulations of spherically symmetric configurations. For the initial condition, we employ the spatial gradient expansion and provide the general form of the growing mode solutions valid up through the second order in this expansion.

arxiv-2410-18297.title: A Pilot Study on Clinician-AI Collaboration in Diagnosing Depression from Speech Thanks: This work was supported by the National Science Foundation (CAREER: Enabling Trustworthy Speech Technologies for Mental Health Care: From Speech Anonymization to Fair Human-centered Machine Intelligence, #204611
arxiv-2410-18297.creator: Kexin Feng, Theodora Chaspari
arxiv-2410-18297.description: Abstract This study investigates clinicians’ perceptions and attitudes toward an assistive artificial intelligence (AI) system that employs a speech-based explainable ML algorithm for detecting depression. The AI system detects depression from vowel-based spectrotemporal variations of speech and generates explanations through explainable AI (XAI) methods.

arxiv-2503-11527.title: Data-Driven Construction of Age-Structured Contact Networks
arxiv-2503-11527.creator: Luke Murray Kearney Orcid, Emma Davis, Matt Keeling
arxiv-2503-11527.description: Abstract Capturing the structure of a population and characterising contacts within the population are key to reliable projections of infectious disease. Two main elements of population structure – contact heterogeneity and age – have been repeatedly demonstrated to be key in infection dynamics, yet are rarely combined.

arxiv-2511-00384.title: Physics-informed digital twins of brainbots
arxiv-2511-00384.creator: I. Mammadli, J. Pande ∗, M. Noirhomme, F. Novkoski, A. Maier, N. Vandewalle, A.-S. Smith †
arxiv-2511-00384.description: Abstract A brainbot is a robotic device powered by a battery-driven motor that induces horizontal vibrations which lead to controlled two-dimensional motion. While the physical design and capabilities of a brainbot have been discussed in previous work, here we present a detailed theoretical analysis of its motion.

pmc-10550613.title: Contribution of compositional changes in the workforce to sickness absence trends in Finland
pmc-10550613.creator: Laura Salonen, Elli Hartikainen, Svetlana Solovieva, Eira Viikari-Juntura, Taina Leinonen
pmc-10550613.description: In this study, we assessed whether the long-term decrease in sickness absences in Finland is explained by observed and unobserved compositional changes in the workforce. Utilizing register-based panel data on Finnish wage earners aged 30–62, we examined the annual onset of compensated sickness absence (granted after 10 weekdays) in the period 2005–2016.

pmc-11591365.title: Brighton v RSPCA NSW: Appeals and Lessons Four Years On
pmc-11591365.creator: Kathryn Jurd, Sophie Riley, Laura A Reese
pmc-11591365.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryOn 14 January 2016, Daniel Brighton killed one of two dogs that had strayed onto his property, where they had attacked Alice, a camel owned by a Petting Zoo business operated by Brighton. In late August 2017, the Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals, New South Wales (RSPCA) became aware of the allegations, commenced an investigation, and thereafter preferred charges in the NSW Local Court at Campbelltown.

pmc-11654024.title: The trials and triumphs of co-producing an evaluation plan: A principles-focused evaluation
pmc-11654024.creator: Holly Harris, Kayle Donner, Jordana Rovet, Elizabeth Rosell, Jacob Wolframe, Taryn Lee, Gail Bellissimo, Andrew Johnson, Sophie Soklaridis, Faisal Islam
pmc-11654024.description: BackgroundRecovery Colleges are mental health-oriented education programs that are rooted in principles of peer support and co-production. Co-production, in this context, involves people with lived experience of mental health and addiction challenges and people with other forms of expertise (e.g., mental health professionals, administrators, and researchers) collaborating on the design and actualization of programs and initiatives.

pmc-12457774.title: Different Risk Factors for Lymph Node Metastasis in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma Patients with and without Hashimoto’s Thyroiditis
pmc-12457774.creator: Jiwei Chen, Haifeng Zhong, Yuedong Wang
pmc-12457774.description: ObjectiveThe immune response triggered by Hashimoto’s thyroiditis may influence the progression of papillary thyroid cancer (PTC), such as lymph node metastasis (LNM). The purpose of this study was to study the relationship between clinicopathological features and LNM in PTC patients with and without Hashimoto’s thyroiditis.

pmc-12717160.title: Multi-omic analysis of hepatocellular carcinoma reveals aberrant cis-regulatory changes and dysregulated retrotransposons with prognostic potential
pmc-12717160.creator: Clooney C Y Cheng, Ming Fung Cheung, Ah Young Lee, Qiong Wu, Savio Ho-Chit Chow, Julie Y J Ang, Ignacio Riquelme Medina, Grace Lo, Haoran Wu, Weiqin Yang, Paul B S Lai, Kevin Y Yip, Alfred S Cheng, Danny Leung
pmc-12717160.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common form of primary liver cancer and has limited therapeutic options. Epigenetic dysregulation plays a crucial role in hepatocarcinogenesis; however, its impact on cis-regulatory elements (CREs) and retrotransposons remains underexplored. Here, we investigated the epigenetic changes underlying the aberrant CRE and retrotransposon activity in HCC.

pmc-13388327.title: Dogs and cats as sources of companionship and emotional support in vulnerable animal caregivers
pmc-13388327.creator: Mónica Boada, Thaïs Sánchez, Noe Terrassa, Antoni Bulbena, Jonathan Bowen, Jaume Fatjó
pmc-13388327.description: Social support may be crucial for the health and wellbeing of populations facing adversity, such as homelessness, intimate partner violence, or economic vulnerability. However, vulnerable individuals are usually at a high risk of social exclusion, having restricted social networks and limited social support.

pmc-13458525.title: Prevalence of alexithymia and its association with social media addiction among medical students in Pakistan: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13458525.creator: Muhammad Bilal, Zuhha Tahir, Mudassir Hayat, Ayesha Abdullah, Aun Haider, Muhammad Saad Riasat, Muhammad Afham, Ishaq Oyeshina Sanusi
pmc-13458525.description: Alexithymia, defined as difficulty in identifying, describing, and expressing emotions, has gained increasing attention in populations exposed to high psychological and academic stress. Medical students represent a particularly vulnerable group due to intensive coursework, emotionally challenging clinical exposure, and the early requirement to adopt professional roles.

pmc-13496057.title: Seasonal variation in wind speed and oceanic salt spray favors delayed reproduction in coastal yellow monkeyflowers
pmc-13496057.creator: Katherine Toll, Chloe Crockett, Lauren Tocci, David B Lowry
pmc-13496057.description: PremiseThe optimal timing of reproduction depends on the relative risk and benefit of continued growth. These risks and benefits depend on the local environment, which varies seasonally. While temperature and water availability are well‐studied selective agents on reproductive timing, less is known about other seasonally variable factors.

pmc-13525311.title: Medial Meniscal Transplant Allograft Using A Hybrid Root Fixation Technique
pmc-13525311.creator: Romed P. Vieider, Vince Morgan, Sahil Dadoo, Robert E. Bilodeau, Shohei Yamauchi, Seth L. Sherman, Volker Musahl
pmc-13525311.description: Background:High rates of osteoarthritis have been reported after partial and total meniscectomy, attributed to increased joint contact stresses in meniscus-deficient knees. Meniscal allograft transplantation (MAT) with hybrid root fixation has emerged as a treatment for meniscal deficiency, combining the advantages of bony and all-soft-tissue techniques.
